newsitem.title: USA: Blue chips end winning streak; broader market sets new highs.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips end winning streak; broader market sets new highs.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks snapped a six session-run of record highs Monday, posting a small loss ahead of a report on May retail inflation, but the broader market still racked up new highs.

In moderate trading, the Dow Jones industrials average ended down 9.95 points at 7,772.09, slipping below Friday's record finish of 7,782.04. Declining issues led advances 1,239 to 1,227 on volume of 414 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The index of 30-blue chip stocks had jumped 477 points, or 6.5 percent as Wall Street celebrated good news that the economy was not overheating and inflation was still in check.
"Even God rested on the seventh day," said Charles White, managing director at Avatar Associates.
But whatever profit taking there was in blue chips did not spread to the broader market.
The strongest of the major indexes was the Nasdaq composite index, which rose 8.92 points to 1,431.95, its second record closing in a row.
The Standard & Poor's 500 index managed a gain of 0.63 of a point to 893.90, its seventh consecutive record finish.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 8,419.854, up 9.929, or 0.12 percent.
Buying in high-technology stocks, which had lagged the recent rally in blue chips, lifted the Nasdaq market.
"You're seeing a rally in the big-cap high tech names," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray & Co.
Among the winners, Intel Corp. rose 2-1/2 to 147-1/4 and Microsoft Corp. added 1-3/4 to 131-3/8.

Investors chose to take some profits ahead of Tuesday's report on the May Consumer Price Index. But after last week's report of soft retail sales and producer prices, there was little concern that the CPI would show inflationary pressures, analysts said.
"The PPI number last week put a lot of people at ease," White said. "The retail sales numbers have put a lot of people at ease."
The government reported last week that producer prices fell for the fifth straight month in May, dropping by 0.3 percent.
It was the first time in 45 years that wholesale prices have dropped for five consecutive months. The May decline followed a whopping 0.6 percent price drop in April.

Some of that confidence was shown in the inflation-sensitive bond market, where the 30-year Treasury bond rose 13/32, or $4.0625 on a $1,000 bond, sending its yield down to 6.69 percent from 6.73 percent on Friday. The price and the yield move in opposite directions.
Traders said they expected news on corporate profits to be the focus for Wall Street in the coming weeks.
Given the recent rally, investors will likely be quick to dump stocks in companies giving any indications that their earnings will not meet expectations.
"Shoot first and ask questions later, that's going to be the modus operandi," said Guy Truicko, equity portfolio manager at Unity Management.

Dell Computer Corp.'s stock jumped 4-1/4 to 115-3/8 after the company's vice chairman said in an interview that Dell's momentum remains strong and the company is "very pleased" with the current quarter and the momentum in the direct-sales PC business.
Compaq Computer Corp. shared in the rally, rising 5 to 105-1/4.

Merrill Lynch downgraded its near-term ratings on several health maintenance organisation companies. Among them, Aetna Inc. fell 3-1/4 to 109-1/2, United HealthCare Corp. dropped 2-1/4 to 54-1/8 and WellPoint Health Networks Inc. was off 1-7/8 to 48-7/8.

Shares in Italian apparel and footware company Fila Holdings SpA tumbled 4-1/2 to 32-7/8 on the New York Stock Exchange, clipped by a company forecast that its second-quarter earnings would be below analysts' expectations.
Anchor Gaming jumped 2-3/8 to 40 after saying that, based on preliminary internal financial reports for April and May, analysts' estimates for its current quarterly profits may be "conservative."
The American Stock Exchange index was off 1.93 to 628.17. The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 0.16 to 465.01. The average share was down 1 cent.
